messages.text:
"Create a first-person shooter roguelite with RPG progression, set in a post-apocalyptic Russian city. Gritty, darkly humorous tone. Visual style: dirty realism, muted palette (gray, blue, dirty yellow), no cyberpunk. Inspired by Hotline Miami, Enter the Gungeon, Skul, Gunfire Reborn.

PLAYER: A tired guy in a hoodie and sneakers. Sprint, dodge roll, slide. FPS shooting, fast reload, kick (stuns and knocks back enemies). No melee weapons. Health 100, out-of-combat regen plus small heal per kill. Status effects on enemies: stun, burning, freezing, bleeding.

WEAPONS: All weapons are improvised from household junk (no real guns). Three classes: Strength (slow, powerful), Balance (versatile), Agility (fast, weak). Examples: paint roller (splashes elemental paint), construction stapler, angle grinder, extension cord with plug (electric shock), toaster (shoots red-hot bolts), blowtorch, kettle, gas canister. Starter weapon \"Leaky Pipe\": infinite ammo, low damage, cannot be upgraded. Rarity: Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary. Upgraded at the Blacksmith for scrap metal; each rank changes the visual model. Weapon upgrades reset on death to force experimentation. Some weapons start at Common, others start at Rare.

WORLD (beta route): Center, Industrial Zone, Residential District, Port. Each ends with a boss. After each boss, a room contains two NPCs: Blacksmith and Dispatcher.

KEYS: To unlock the next location, find a key in the current location and carry it to the end. If you die holding a key, it is lost and respawns elsewhere. Hand keys to the Dispatcher after the boss.

ECONOMY, THREE CURRENCIES:
1. Credits (in-run): from enemies. Spent on chests. Leftovers after a boss convert to max HP (1 credit = 0.5% HP, capped at +25% per stage).
2. Scrap Metal (in-run): only from dismantling unwanted weapons. Spent at the Blacksmith to upgrade your weapon. Lost on death.
3. Components (meta): from bosses, secret rooms, challenges. Persist between runs. Spent at the Dispatcher to permanently unlock new weapons, passive items, skins, enemy factions, and starting bonuses.

CHESTS, 4 color-coded tiers: Common (gray, mostly common loot), Rare (green, mostly rare loot), Epic (purple, mostly epic loot), Legendary (gold, guaranteed legendary plus 2 passive items). Chest prices scale with stage. Credit drops are capped per stage at the total cost of all chests plus a 10% bonus.

ENEMIES: Factions include Rusted (zombies), Stalkers (raiders), Mutants, Robots, Bandits, Deep Ones. Center has 3 types (melee, ranged, heavy). Later stages add flying, buffer, spawner, bomber. Elites appear from stage 3 with immunities and bonus loot.

BOSSES: Center tutorial mini-boss. Industrial Zone: \"Craneman\", a giant built from pipes and conveyors with a crane arm; phase 2 he magnetically pulls in scrap and gets aggressive; weak spots are hydraulics and exposed wires. Residential District: \"Mad Dog\", a fast mutant with floor traps. Port: \"Deep Leviathan\", 3 phases with a weak point and summoned waves.

NPCs:
- Blacksmith: bearded man in a leather apron at an anvil. Upgrades weapons for scrap metal, striking them with a hammer; sparks fly in the color of the new rarity and the model transforms.
- Dispatcher: old technician at a desk with city maps. Accepts keys to permanently unlock locations, gives hints on key locations, and sells permanent unlocks for Components.

CHALLENGES: Automatic achievements (kill 1000 enemies, beat a boss without damage, find secret rooms) that directly grant weapons, items, or skins without any currency.

PROTOTYPE SCOPE: one location (Center), 3 enemy types, 1 mini-boss, the starter Leaky Pipe, basic chests and credits, basic movement (sprint, dodge roll, kick). Exclude: melee weapons, cyberpunk, complex story, open world, multiplayer, persistent weapon upgrades between runs.

Build a playable vertical slice: movement, shooting, enemy AI, chest interaction, currency pickup, and a boss fight in the Center location. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
